Row.Text: The [B]Theodosian Walls[/B] kept [B]Byzantium[/B] standing for a thousand years.
Behind their walls the {1_Civilization_Adj} people have learned patience. Sieges come and go; the markets reopen, the mosaics are restored, and the city on the strait endures.
[B]Byzantium[/B] is able to endure throughout the Ages.
[B]Russia[/B] claimed the legacy of [B]Byzantium[/B] as the Third Rome.
The [B]Ottomans[/B] took Constantinople and ruled from [B]Byzantium's[/B] capital.
[B]Byzantium[/B] was the eastern half of [B]Rome[/B], and outlived the western.
[B]Byzantium[/B] spoke Greek and inherited the cities of [B]Greece[/B].
[B]Augustus[/B] founded the empire that [B]Byzantium[/B] carried on.
[B]Charlemagne[/B] and [B]Byzantium[/B] disputed the title of Roman Emperor.
[B]Xerxes[/B] ruled the lands [B]Byzantium[/B] would contest with Persia for centuries.
